scenes.title: The Ridiculous
scenes.summary: Comedy imitates the worse, not in every vice but in the ridiculous, a part of the ugly: a fault that causes no pain or harm, like the comic mask.

scenes.title: The Lost History of Comedy
scenes.summary: Comedy was not taken seriously, so its beginnings are unknown: the archon granted a comic chorus only late; plots began in Sicily, and Crates was the first at Athens to give up lampoon.

scenes.title: Epic and Tragedy
scenes.summary: Epic shares with tragedy the imitation of serious people in verse, but differs in its single meter, its narration and its length: tragedy keeps to one circuit of the sun.
